note: NEW-008 / NEW-009: an ANF bigint const ABOVE 2^53 — serialised on disk as the string "9007199254740993n" — feeding a length-sensitive byte op. The fixture pins bytes; this spec pins what those bytes DO. `~(9007199254740993n << 8n)` is -2305843009213694209 under native BigInt semantics, but on chain 9007199254740993 is the 7-byte script number 01000000000020, OP_LSHIFT is LENGTH-PRESERVING (00000000002000, a non-minimal 7-byte 2^45, NEW-004), and OP_INVERT then flips all seven bytes to ffffffffffdfff = -35993612646875135. The expectedState pin below is that hand-derived on-chain value, NOT the BigInt one — so a tier that takes the ByteString path for an n-string operand (NEW-008), or re-minimises anywhere along shift->invert (NEW-004), or rounds the const through float64 (NEW-009), lands on a different number and fails here even though every tier still agrees on the golden bytes. Cannot be a plain witnesses/*.json differential spec: this is the only witnessed StatefulSmartContract, and that harness pushes method args only, so the compiler-injected checkPreimage finds an empty stack (OP_DUP on an empty stack) and the run diverges before reaching the shift.
